laws.rule: Galway County Council Beach Bye-Laws 1997 apply to the scheduled beaches in the county health district, including Furbo, Spiddal and nearby strands, Tracht at Kinvara, Clifden, Gurteen and Dogs Bay at Roundstone, Trá an Doilin at An Cheathrú Rua, Kilmurvey on Inis Mór, the beach on Inisheer, Barna, Omey, Cleggan and several Renvyle strands. On those beaches it is forbidden to light a fire, damage dunes or plants, act in a disorderly or offensive way, play music so as to cause a nuisance, use a bicycle or any mechanically propelled vehicle, bring a horse or similar animal, camp or erect a tent or caravan, park a camper or caravan overnight on a road or car park at the beach, or place objects for sale or hire (including kayaks, surfboards and jet skis) without a council licence. Jet skis and fast power boats must not be used within 200 metres of the water's edge except for rescue. A person who contravenes the bye-laws is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding one thousand pounds (the 1997 official text; a later euro equivalent may apply). An authorised person can require someone to stop, remove them if they do not, and demand their name and address.
